page: Google Cloud Platform m4n-megamem-224 is an x86_64 architecture server within the m4n instance family. It features 224 dedicated virtual central processing units (vCPUs) and 2976.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a high memory-to-core ratio of approximately 13.29 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include local storage or integrated graphics processing units (GPUs), and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The primary architectural characteristic of this server is its massive memory capacity, designed for workloads requiring large datasets to reside entirely in system memory. Because there is no bundled local storage, all storage operations must rely on network-attached persistent disks or external storage services. The lack of hardware accelerators like GPUs limits its utility for direct machine learning training or graphics rendering tasks, positioning the hardware resources entirely toward memory-bound CPU workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m4n-megamem-224 represents a high-density resource allocation where the cost is concentrated on massive RAM capacity and a high core count. This resource profile is optimized for large-scale enterprise applications, such as massive in-memory databases, SAP HANA workloads, large-scale data analytics, and complex enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems that demand substantial memory footprints without requiring local physical disks or GPU acceleration.
